page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.2xlarge is a burstable instance type built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 8 virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a performance profile characterized by modest single-core capabilities and moderate multi-core capacity. Single-core performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core, place the instance in the bottom 10% tier. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests, reach average levels in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached reads also perform in the average tier, though database operations and static web serving throughput show weaker results, falling into the bottom 25% tier.

As a burstable instance, the ecs.t5-c1m2.2xlarge offers a cost-effective profile for workloads that do not require continuous high CPU utilization. The primary tradeoff is the CPU credit system inherent to the burstable allocation model; sustained high-intensity workloads will deplete credits, leading to throttled performance. This makes the instance highly resource-efficient for baseline operations with occasional spikes, but inefficient for continuous heavy compute tasks.

This instance is best suited for low-traffic web servers, development and testing environments, microservices, and light background tasks. It is also appropriate for code compilation and basic text processing tasks that can tolerate variable CPU performance.
